title: Lesson 71 - Here's the Evidence I Found

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Here’s the evidence I found: an eight-week log, an observer note covering three meetings and a pulse survey completed by nine of the twelve team members.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Before choosing evidence, what exact claim are we trying to support?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: “The bundled process made action ownership more visible in this support team.” That is narrower than saying it improved all performance.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Good. The evidence most relevant to ownership is the log showing that every new action had a named owner from week two onward.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The observer note, written by a facilitator who attended weeks three, five and seven, records that owners were stated aloud for fourteen of fifteen new actions.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Those two sources describe the process from different angles: the stored record and what happened in meetings.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The participants who answered the survey also reported greater clarity: seven of nine agreed that they knew who would follow up after the shorter check-ins.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Useful, but it is self-report. It supports perceived clarity among respondents, not proof that every owner completed the action.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Should we include the drop from ten to six overdue items?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: As context, yes. It is an outcome recorded during the same period, but it cannot isolate ownership from shorter meetings, the agenda, review or workload.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: What evidence is not relevant enough for this briefing?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: The survey item saying six people found the meetings “less tiring.” That matters to experience, but it does not directly support action visibility.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: And the average meeting length falling from twenty-nine to sixteen minutes?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: It confirms that the format changed, but shorter duration alone does not show clearer ownership. We can mention it only to describe the bundle.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Taken together, these findings support a limited conclusion: owners were more consistently named and most survey respondents perceived follow-up as clearer.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Add the outcome carefully: recorded overdue items also declined, although the sources cannot tell us how much ownership contributed.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The main limitation affecting the conclusion is that all three sources concern the same twelve-person team.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: There are two more: only three meetings were observed, and three team members did not answer the survey.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Then I’ll use one sentence per evidence type—record, observation and self-report—followed immediately by the shared sample limit.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Exactly. Strong evidence communication makes the relevance visible and the limitation hard to miss.
